page.title: Completion and final inspections
page.body:
Completion and final inspections


The culmination of your Andalusian dream home is within reach! With construction nearing completion, it’s time to focus on the final details and the crucial final inspection. This guide equips you with the knowledge to navigate this exciting stage smoothly.


The Final Stretch: Touch-Ups and Quality Checks


Punch List Creation: Collaborate with your architect and contractor to create a comprehensive punch list. This detailed document should include all outstanding items requiring completion, from minor touch-ups (paint nicks, imperfect tile work) to the installation of final fixtures (light fixtures, faucets).

Quality Control Inspections: Conduct regular walkthroughs with your architect to identify and address any quality control issues before they become bigger problems. Pay attention to details like:

  • Finishes: Ensure paintwork is smooth and consistent, flooring is level and free of defects, and tilework is properly aligned.
  • Plumbing and Electrical Systems: Test all faucets, toilets, showers, and electrical outlets for proper functionality.
  • Doors and Windows: Confirm smooth operation of doors and windows, ensuring proper sealing and weatherproofing.


The Big Day: Final Inspection and Approvals


Schedule the Inspection: Once construction is complete and the punch list is addressed, work with your architect to schedule the final inspection with the local municipal technical department.

Documentation at Hand: Ensure you have all the necessary documentation readily available for the inspection, including:

  • Building permits
  • Approved construction plans
  • Certificates for materials used (if required)


The Inspection Process 

The inspector will thoroughly examine the building to ensure compliance with all regulations and permits. They will check aspects like:

  • Structural integrity
  • Fire safety measures
  • Accessibility features
  • Energy efficiency compliance
  • Adherence to approved plans


Addressing Issues and Obtaining the Cédula de Habitabilidad


Potential Revisions: If the inspector identifies any non-compliance issues, they will outline the necessary corrections. Work with your contractor to address these promptly.

The Final Hurdle: Once all concerns are rectified and the inspector grants approval, you can obtain the “cédula de habitabilidad” (occupancy certificate) from the town hall. This crucial document is mandatory to legally occupy the building.


Additional Tips:


Clear Communication: Maintain clear communication with your architect and contractor throughout the final stages. This ensures everyone is on the same page regarding punch list completion, inspection scheduling, and addressing any potential issues.

Celebrate Milestones: Don’t forget to celebrate milestones along the way! Completing the punch list and successfully passing the final inspection are significant achievements on your journey to enjoying your dream home.

Post-Construction Warranties: Before finalising payments, ensure you receive all necessary warranties for materials and workmanship from your contractor. These will provide peace of mind and protect you in case of any issues arising after completion.


By following these steps and prioritising clear communication with your architect and contractor, you can navigate the completion and final inspection stage with confidence. Soon, you’ll be basking in the joy of receiving your occupancy certificate and finally calling your beautiful Andalusian dream home your own!
